newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks sharply lower amid renewed rate fears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks sharply lower amid renewed rate fears.

text.p: U.S. stocks were sharply lower at midsession on Friday after stronger-than-expected economic data convinced many market players that Wall Street was facing further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
The Dow was off about 80 points, or 1.2 percent, at 6459 after tumbling to a morning low of 6449. Big Board losers were crushing gainers by a 20-to-three ratio.
"Today's numbers have sort of rekindled the fear that (Fed chairman Alan) Greenspan will have to act," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray and Co.
The Nasdaq composite sank about 19 points, or 1.5 percent, to 1217. The S&P 500 index was also off 1.5 percent, falling 11 points to 747.
Stocks were unnerved by bonds' reaction to the economic date. The 30-year Treasury bond was off 24/32, its yield climbing to 7.18 percent from Thursday's close at 7.11

Analysts said said stronger-than-expected core March producer price data and an upward revision to February retail sales further convinced market players that the Fed would act at its May 20 policy-making meeting to boost interest rates.
Some had harbored hopes that the March 25 Fed rate hike would be all the tightening needed to keep inflation in check.
"I don't think there's really too many shreds of good news in the data for people who thought that the Fed was going to be 'one-and-done'," said Charles White, managing director, Avatar Associates.

The Labor Department said producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March after dropping 0.4 percent in February. But the so-called core rate, excluding volatile food and energy components, it rose 0.4 percent versus a 0.1 percent fall in the previous month.
Economists in a Reuters poll forecasted, on average, the PPI to be unchanged in March. The PPI without the food and energy components was expected to be up 0.1 percent.

Meanwhile, the Commerce Department said retail sales rose 0.2 percent in March compared to a revised 1.5-percent increase in February. Retail sales had been expected to rise 0.6 percent after an original February reading of a 0.8 percent rise.
Technical analysts have said they expect U.S. stocks to retest their lows set last week at around 6400 before any rallies.
Technology stocks again led Wall Street's downdraft.
Traders said investors were jittery ahead of Intel Corp's quarterly earnings report Monday and speculation Intel will make deeper-than-usual price cuts in its Pentium chips.
Intel was off 3-3/4 to 133-1/2, Advanced Micro Devices Inc fell 1-1/4 to 38-3/8 and Texas Instruments Inc lost 1-1/8 to 81-1/2.
Boston Scientific Corp tumbled 14-3/4 to 45-3/4 after the medical device maker said its first quarter earnings would fall short of analysts' expectations.
Shares of Loehmann's Inc fell 2-1/4 to 8-5/8 after the retailer said it expected quarterly earnings to fall well below expectations.
